sub_scenario.one_line: pharmacovigilance reviewer: require written observed, reasonred, and unconfirmed notes first

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the pharmacovigilance reviewer and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I give routine status updates calmly from a checklist. Case-note 577.
Routine reporting is not ownership. Case-note 578.
Ownership under ambiguity is different. Case-note 579.
Someone new shadowed me in the workplace this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the review cycle into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
For a safety signal, I write observed and unconfirmed notes before accepting ownership. Case-note 583.
The written separation prevents overclaiming. Case-note 584.
It makes the handoff carefully bounded. Case-note 585.
A normal daytime update has plenty of follow-up time. Case-note 580.
The bridge has no spare discussion window. Case-note 581.
That is why format matters. Case-note 582.
I archived last cycle's notes on the calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Only the 06:10 APAC bridge overlaps this week. Case-note 586.
The early bridge is the sole demand slot. Case-note 587.
There is no later repair conversation. Case-note 588.
A vendor call about the pharmacovigilance reviewer ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the workplace checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the review cycle.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
When logs were absent during a prior safety signal, verbal ownership named the wrong cause. Case-note 589.
That decision triggered an unnecessary rollback. Case-note 590.
I had spoken before the record arrived. Case-note 591.
I sketched next week's plan for the review cycle before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the pharmacovigilance reviewer updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
A written signal note lets the partner see what is known and unknown. Case-note 592.
The document changes the handoff method. Case-note 593.
It is not merely a preference. Case-note 594.
I compared two options for the calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the workplace handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The partner lead asks me to take 06:10 APAC bridge verbal ownership of a safety signal while incomplete case file may remain. How should I reply?
